title: improv·artist · chromatic (Gerhard Richter)
mutation_directive: improv artist: chromatic via Gerhard Richter

improv_extras.practice: color-grid charts, squeegee abstracts; randomness as method

v1.feedback: The Richter idea registers as color-banded tube rather than true squeegee abstraction — the band transitions use a simple smoothstep blend when they should simulate horizontal paint-drag with directional smearing and variable-width bleeding between adjacent bands. Increase the squeegee displacement amplitude and add a horizontal wobble term (world XZ angle-dependent) so bands appear physically dragged across the surface rather than cleanly UV-mapped. The differential growth form is solid and fills frame well, but the shader needs a second pass: mix adjacent band colors with a noise-driven lerp that varies along the tube circumference to break the uniformity and sell the oil-paint materiality.

v2.feedback: The Richter palette is well-chosen and the squeegee displacement via FBM-shifted band boundaries is a genuine translation of his technique onto a 3D form. Two things to tighten: the smoothstep blend width (0.08) is too clean — Richter's squeegee leaves ragged, overlapping paint ridges, so add a second noise pass to break up the band edges irregularly. Second, the slow uTime animation makes the color feel like a scrolling rainbow rather than a frozen squeegee moment — consider freezing the squeegee phase and letting only the differential growth animate, which would better honor how Richter's abstracts capture a single decisive drag.
